questions.question: What does a reaction rate describe?
choices: How quickly reactants are consumed or products form
The total amount of product at equilibrium
The energy difference between reactants and products
The number of atoms in a reactant molecule

questions.question: What is activation energy?
choices: The energy barrier for a reaction pathway
The energy stored only in products
The total heat released by any reaction
The energy needed to weigh a substance

questions.question: What is a reaction inhibitor?
choices: A substance that always lowers the activation barrier
A substance that must become the main product
A substance that reduces a reaction's rate
A substance that guarantees a higher equilibrium product amount

questions.question: Which unit can describe change in concentration over time?
choices: Grams per cubic centimeter
Mol per liter per second
Joules per kelvin
Liters per mole

questions.question: According to collision theory, what is required for a successful reactive collision?
choices: Enough energy regardless of particle orientation
Correct orientation regardless of collision energy
High concentration without any collisions
Enough energy and suitable orientation

questions.question: What is an enzyme?
choices: A reaction's final product
A biological storage carbohydrate
A biological catalyst
A molecule that supplies all reaction energy

questions.question: What does a reaction-rate graph of product amount against time show through its slope?
choices: The rate at which product amount changes
The total reactant mass at every instant
The reaction's equilibrium constant
The temperature difference between reactants and products

questions.question: Why does higher temperature usually speed up a reaction?
choices: All collisions become successful regardless of orientation
The reactants gain more total particles solely from heating
The reaction's activation barrier must become zero
More particles can overcome the activation-energy barrier

questions.question: Why can increased reactant concentration increase reaction rate?
choices: The number of possible collisions decreases
Reactant particles collide more frequently
Each particle must gain more kinetic energy at fixed temperature
The equilibrium amount of product necessarily doubles

questions.question: Why can powdered limestone react faster than an equal mass of large limestone pieces?
choices: The powder has greater total mass in this comparison
More solid surface contacts the reacting solution
Powdering changes the chemical composition of the limestone
The powder lowers the acid concentration before contact

questions.question: How does a catalyst provide a faster reaction pathway?
choices: It increases the required activation energy
It raises every reactant's kinetic energy at fixed temperature
It changes the equilibrium constant at fixed temperature
It lowers the activation-energy barrier

questions.question: Why does cooling often slow a reaction?
choices: Fewer collisions have enough energy to react
The activation energy must disappear
Every reacting particle stops moving
The number of particles necessarily falls to zero

questions.question: Why can reaction rate decrease as a reactant is used up?
choices: Product concentration must stay zero
The remaining particles stop colliding
Lower reactant concentration can reduce successful collisions
Reactant concentration has no effect on collision frequency

questions.question: Why might an enzyme lose activity after strong heating?
choices: The enzyme's active site always becomes more effective
The enzyme gains more substrate-binding sites automatically
The enzyme's concentration necessarily doubles
Its shape can change, affecting its active site

questions.question: Does a catalyst necessarily increase the amount of product present at equilibrium?
choices: Yes, it always doubles the final product amount
Yes, it removes the reverse reaction
No, it mainly speeds approach to equilibrium
No, it prevents any product from forming

questions.question: A reaction forms 12 mL of gas in 3 seconds. What is its average gas-production rate?
choices: 4 mL/s
36 mL/s
9 mL/s

questions.question: Which experiment best tests the effect of temperature on a reaction rate?
choices: Change temperature and concentration together
Keep concentrations and amounts the same while changing temperature
Use different reactants at each temperature
Compare only the final colors

questions.question: Two gas-volume curves reach the same final volume, but one rises more steeply at first. What does this show?
choices: The steeper curve necessarily reaches a greater final volume
The gentler curve initially has the higher production rate
Equal final volume requires identical rates at every time
One reaction initially produces gas faster

questions.question: A student compares powder and chunks of the same solid. Which quantity should be held constant to isolate surface area?
choices: Shape of each piece
Total mass of solid
Number of exposed surfaces
Dissolving time

questions.question: An enzyme works best near 37°C and less well at 70°C. Which explanation fits these observations?
choices: Increasing temperature always slows all reactions
Enzymes cannot function in liquids
High temperature can disrupt the enzyme's functional shape
The substrate necessarily becomes radioactive
